ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PESISIR SELATAN REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As an asset and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee their implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive measures must be taken so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 of 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included children's rights, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of women's and children's constitutional rights and the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Article 2

What is meant by gender justice is fair conditions and treatment of women and men, so that justice for women and men is realized, steps are needed to stop things that politically and socio-culturally can hinder women and men from being able to play a role and enjoy the results of their role.

Point c What is meant by non-discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence they experience, no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.

Point e What is meant by the best interests of women and children is that in all actions concerning women and children carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of women and children must be a primary consideration.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Pesisir Selatan
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pesisir Selatan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Pesisir Selatan Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Pesisir Selatan Regency.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
28. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As an asset and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee their implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive measures must be taken so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 of 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included children's rights, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of women's and children's constitutional rights and the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

1. The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. Regional Government guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:a. guidelines and standards for fulfillment, by facilitating the formation of policies and regulations that serve as guidelines and standards in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.
b. technical guidance and training, including:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each OPD for the preparation of activity programs based on gender responsive planning and budgeting.
c. Provision of facilities, the Regional Government provides facilities, means and infrastructure in implementing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the formation of nagari that care for women and children; e. Provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
3. Supervision conducted by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:a. Monitoring, in the form of:
1. OPD Leaders in accordance with their duties and functions are obligated to submit reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs to the Regent.
2. Reports as referred to shall be submitted periodically once every 3 (three) months.
b. Evaluation, conducted in the form of:
1. The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once every 3 (three) months.
2. In conducting supervision and evaluation, the Regent may appoint OPDs in accordance with their duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation serve as evaluation material for women's empowerment and child protection program policies.
4. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) in order to realize the objectives of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Pesisir Selatan
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pesisir Selatan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Pesisir Selatan Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Pesisir Selatan Regency.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
28. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by promotive aspect is to increase so that health status becomes increasingly improved, for example providing early breastfeeding initiation (IMD) and exclusive breastfeeding which can help increase immunity to disease because of colostrum and nutrients contained in breast milk, so that children are not easily affected by disease.

Letter b What is meant by preventive aspect is to prevent from contracting disease or to keep healthy people healthy, for example washing hands before eating and after defecating will prevent the occurrence of diarrhea.

Letter c What is meant by curative aspect is the process of curing a person from a state of physical and psychological illness.

Letter d What is meant by rehabilitative aspect is the process of maintaining so that a person who has recovered (not yet 100% recovered) returns to being fit as before.

Paragraph (2) What is meant by health rehabilitation conducted comprehensively is health rehabilitation conducted in a promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative manner and able to respond.

Paragraph (3) Letter a What is meant by medical services is services provided to reduce impact and prevent further injury, suffering and cost threats. including:

1. physical examination and treatment of physical injuries;
2. treatment of psychological disorders;
3. treatment for prevention of sexually transmitted diseases;
4. treatment for HIV prevention; and
5. reproductive health services.

Article 28

Article 24

1. The implementation of UPTD PPA services is integrative, either in the form of one roof or networked to provide optimal services to women and children who experience problems.
2. In the event that the implementation of integrated services is carried out under one roof, UPTD PPA is responsible for carrying out the entire process in one unit to provide the services needed by women and children who experience problems.
3. In the event that the implementation of integrated services is carried out in a networked manner, UPTD PPA is responsible for the entire referral process for services needed by women and children who experience problems.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. 3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 24

1. The implementation of UPTD PPA services is integrative, either in the form of one roof or networked to provide optimal services to women and children who experience problems.
2. In the event that the implementation of integrated services is carried out under one roof, UPTD PPA is responsible for carrying out the entire process in one unit to provide the services needed by women and children who experience problems.

Article 28

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article Article 23 paragraph (3) letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women and children who experience social dysfunction due to criminal and/or civil matters to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services for:a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; andc. spiritual guidance.

CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

General

Article 30

1. The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil matters.
2. Safe house provision services aim to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil matters from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil matters who require safe houses include: a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/ord. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 32

1. Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) letter f constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil matters concerning women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
3. Types of legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of investigation reports;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process at court; d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; ande. legal assistance in the mediation process.
4. The Regional Government shall provide legal assistance to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil matters based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
5. In providing legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3) UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other gender-sensitive legal assistants.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by respect for the rights of women and children as regulated by laws and regulations concerning the rights of women and children.

Point b What is meant by gender equality is the equality of conditions and positions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, educational, defense, national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development with balanced impacts.

What is meant by gender justice is fair conditions and treatment of women and men, so that justice for women and men is realized, steps are needed to stop things that politically and socio-culturally can hinder women and men from being able to play a role and enjoy the results of their role.

Point c What is meant by non-discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence they experience, no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.

Point d What is meant by local wisdom is good cultural values that exist within a community.

Point e What is meant by the best interests of women and children is that in all actions concerning women and children carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of women and children must be a primary consideration.

CHAPTER IX

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 69

In order to ensure effectiveness and efficiency in the implementation of protection services for women and children, before the UPTD PPA is formed, the duties and functions of the UPTD PPA shall be carried out by the OPD that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Part Three

Effectiveness of Services for Women and Children

Article 26

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/orc. by letter.
3. In addition to complaint services submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 25 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 17

1. Community participation in efforts to Protect Women and Children:  a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and c. monitor the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 28

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article Article 23 paragraph (3) letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women and children who experience social dysfunction due to criminal and/or civil matters to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services for:a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; andc. spiritual guidance.
3. The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) UPTD PPA may cooperate with women crisis centres and/or social community organizations that already exist.

Article 34

1. Social reintegration shall be conducted in order to reunite women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil matters with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
2. Social reintegration is aimed so that:a. women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil matters can resume their social life; and b. women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil matters can have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 21

In order to prevent acts of violence against women and children, the community:
a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violations of the rights of women and children; b. increases awareness of violations of the rights of women and children;
c. strengthens the role of community, religious and family environment organizations; andd. prevents unregistered marriages and marriage at the age of children.

CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 67

1. The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. Regional Government guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:a. guidelines and standards for fulfillment, by facilitating the formation of policies and regulations that serve as guidelines and standards in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.
b. technical guidance and training, including:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each OPD for the preparation of activity programs based on gender responsive planning and budgeting.
c. Provision of facilities, the Regional Government provides facilities, means and infrastructure in implementing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the formation of nagari that care for women and children; e. Provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
3. Supervision conducted by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:a. Monitoring, in the form of:
1. OPD Leaders in accordance with their duties and functions are obligated to submit reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs to the Regent.
2. Reports as referred to shall be submitted periodically once every 3 (three) months.
b. Evaluation, conducted in the form of:
1. The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once every 3 (three) months.
2. In conducting supervision and evaluation, the Regent may appoint OPDs in accordance with their duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation serve as evaluation material for women's empowerment and child protection program policies.
4. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) in order to realize the objectives of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As an asset and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee their implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive measures must be taken so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 of 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included children's rights, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of women's and children's constitutional rights and the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PESISIR SELATAN REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As an asset and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee their implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive measures must be taken so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 of 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included children's rights, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of women's and children's constitutional rights and the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Article 26

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/orc. by letter.
3. In addition to complaint services submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 25 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 32

1. Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) letter f constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil matters concerning women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process at court; d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; ande. legal assistance in the mediation process.

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violations of the rights of women and children; b. increases awareness of violations of the rights of women and children;
c. strengthens the role of community, religious and family environment organizations; andd. prevents unregistered marriages and marriage at the age of children.

Article 34

1. Social reintegration shall be conducted in order to reunite women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil matters with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

6. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PESISIR SELATAN REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As an asset and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee their implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive measures must be taken so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 of 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included children's rights, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of women's and children's constitutional rights and the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Part One

General

Article 28

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article Article 23 paragraph (3) letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women and children who experience social dysfunction due to criminal and/or civil matters to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services for:a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; andc. spiritual guidance.
3. The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) UPTD PPA may cooperate with women crisis centres and/or social community organizations that already exist.

Article 30

1. The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil matters.
2. Safe house provision services aim to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil matters from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil matters who require safe houses include: a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/ord. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 32

1. Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) letter f constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil matters concerning women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
3. Types of legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of investigation reports;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process at court; d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; ande. legal assistance in the mediation process.
4. The Regional Government shall provide legal assistance to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil matters based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
5. In providing legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3) UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other gender-sensitive legal assistants.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Pesisir Selatan
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pesisir Selatan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Pesisir Selatan Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Pesisir Selatan Regency.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improving quality of life, and increasing women's participation in development.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
28. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

I. GENERAL

Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As an asset and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee their implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive measures must be taken so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 of 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included children's rights, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of women's and children's rights has been regulated in national-level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of women's and children's constitutional rights and the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

What is meant by gender justice is fair conditions and treatment of women and men, so that justice for women and men is realized, steps are needed to stop things that politically and socio-culturally can hinder women and men from being able to play a role and enjoy the results of their role.

Article 36

CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 67

1. The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. Regional Government guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:a. guidelines and standards for fulfillment, by facilitating the formation of policies and regulations that serve as guidelines and standards in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.
b. technical guidance and training, including:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each OPD for the preparation of activity programs based on gender responsive planning and budgeting.
c. Provision of facilities, the Regional Government provides facilities, means and infrastructure in implementing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the formation of nagari that care for women and children; e. Provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
3. Supervision conducted by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:a. Monitoring, in the form of:
1. OPD Leaders in accordance with their duties and functions are obligated to submit reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs to the Regent.
2. Reports as referred to shall be submitted periodically once every 3 (three) months.
b. Evaluation, conducted in the form of:
1. The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once every 3 (three) months.
2. In conducting supervision and evaluation, the Regent may appoint OPDs in accordance with their duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation serve as evaluation material for women's empowerment and child protection program policies.
4. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) in order to realize the objectives of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 50

Regional Government shall guarantee the implementation of compulsory education programs for Children in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 53

1. Children with disabilities and Children with special needs shall be given equal opportunities to obtain formal, non-formal and informal educational services, including inclusive education programs.
2. Regional government shall provide teaching personnel for inclusive education in every education unit.
